liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Ramble On Rose** (3 reviews): The show really takes off during this song; Crowd and band both woke up at the 'aces back to back' line, the first real engagement [8][10][13]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Opening the second set on the run's first night, this Scarlet is quite long and spacy; Reviewer's first Scarlet>Fire; a bouncy version that stays fairly grounded without going far out [11][15]
- **Black Throated Wind** (1 review): Has a typically nice finale [11]
- **Liberty** (1 review): Band was still finding the right slot for it; it seems better suited to an encore [11]

## The recordings

- **gd1993-05-14.141491.OTS.AKG.Ackerman.Miller.Noel.t-flac.1648** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 152 min [1]
- **gd1993-05-14.sennME80.wklitz.94259.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 154 min; rated 4.33/5 by 6 [2]
- **gd93-05-14.aud.fink.17812.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 139 min; rated 3.79/5 by 14 [7]. Said about its sound: Very good for an audience tape, with Garcia's guitar standing out prominently in the mix [8]
- **gd1993-05-14.112085.schoepsMK41.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 156 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]

## Around the show

- The heat was miserable, though everyone including the band seemed to enjoy that weekend [8]
- Long wait to enter the lot; a sudden thundershower hit and a woman walking to the show was struck by lightning but was okay [10]
- A thunderstorm struck; someone on the field watched a man climbing the stadium lights while lightning was very close [12]
- Heavy traffic forced a long walk; Sting was missed, hail was falling, and fans were told to leave the metal bleachers due to lightning [13]
- Cold Rain started as the day's heat eased; showtime was about 2:30PM on all three days [17]
- A dust and lightning storm came through, especially during the encore [18]
- Wind is jokingly credited as a special guest, referring to Mother Nature [1]
- Preferred this to the other two shows of the run because the keyboardist's synth wash didn't bury Jerry's guitar [9]
- Sting played the same set on Saturday, then changed it up on Sunday with covers [12]
- Reviewer found Jerry using much less MIDI than usual, and the run felt like a tour kick-start [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1993-05-14.141491.OTS.AKG.Ackerman.Miller.Noel.t-flac.1648**: taped by Ray Ackerman; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel; source: flac16/48kHz ; Master Audience Recording & Transfer by Ray Ackerman: AKG 460/61 B18 > AKG B18 phantom power unit > Panasonic SV255 > DAT (OTS); Location: on… [1]
- **gd1993-05-14.sennME80.wklitz.94259.flac16**: taped by Keith Litzenberger; transferred by Keith Litzenberger; source: Sennheiser ME-80's>Technics SV-MD1 (DAT) [2]. Also: Reviewer praises the taping job and says they flew from Maui to Vegas for the shows [16]
- **gd93-05-14.aud.fink.17812.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Paul B. and Alan J. Fink; source: Audience: Unknown Mics [7]. Also: Reviewer once bought a bootleg CD of this show, believed to be a front-of-board source, with audience audibly reacting to a jet [9]
- **gd1993-05-14.112085.schoepsMK41.flac16**: source: Recording Info: FOBH 30' center Schoeps Mk-41 3.5" @ 90* ( 1/2 O.R.T.F ) > Schoeps KC5 Actives > CMC 4 > Canare Star Quad > Koch Power Supply > Canare Star… [3]
